title: Kian's Bug Hotel Village
markdown:
Kian the Measure Master loved measuring everything. His toast? Three whole inches, munch-munch-munch. His speedy running? Ten giant steps, WHOOSH.

So Kian had a brand-new bug hotel, but it was emptier than a cookie jar after a bear convention. “Oh dear,” he sighed. “Nobody’s coming to stay.”

Puddle the frog hopped over. “What’s wrong, Kian?”

“My bug hotel is empty. It looks all bare and lonely.”

“Maybe we need to make it super-duper inviting.”

Kian wriggled his nose. “But what if it’s too plain? Or too drafty? What if they have nowhere cozy to hide?” He looked as if he’d swallowed a whole bag of sour lemons.

Grandma Nell came pottering over from her garden, smelling like sunshine. “Empty bug homes, you say?” She knelt by the hotel.

A different house for a different guest.

“Not all tiny creatures like the same kind of home,” she said, warm as a fuzzy blanket. “It’s like choosing your very own favourite toy.” She pointed to some crinkly leaves. “This ladybug? She loves it dark and cozy in here.” Kian saw a tiny ladybug peeking out. Snug.

Nell pointed to some smooth hollow stems. “And these busy bees love a nice straight tunnel. A teeny-tiny tube hotel.” Kian could almost hear a little buzz. Bzzzzzzzzz.

Kian’s eyes popped. “So they need different kinds of houses? Not just one big house for everyone?”

“Exactly. Some like natural holes. Some like soft straw to snuggle in. Some like pebbles to peek from. It’s about making them feel safe.” She showed him how to measure for what would make them feel just right.

A different house for a different guest.

Kian got out his trusty measuring tape. He measured snug leaf piles. Puddle gathered smooth hollow stems. Plink, plonk. They fit them in place. Kian measured out soft wispy straw. He found twigs with lovely natural holes. Puddle arranged smooth warm pebbles. They worked together, a super-speedy team, zip, zap, zoom.

Soon their bug hotel was a miniature village. A happy bee zipped into a hollow stem with a cheerful Bzzzzzzzz. A ladybug wiggled into a leaf pile. The hotel was alive with tiny movements and happy buzzes.

“Wow!” Puddle ribbit-ed. “It’s full of friends!”

Kian beamed, heart full as a berry bush in summer. “We have to make lots of different kinds of homes, just for them.”

Grandma Nell smiled. “That’s right, my clever Measure Master. A wonderful, welcoming home, full of variety.”

Kian looked at his bustling bug hotel. “Everyone likes their own special place.” He couldn’t wait to see what else the world was hiding. What else could he measure and learn about?

A different house for a different guest.
characters: Kian (a measure master), Puddle (a frog), Nell (a grandma)
